newsitem.title: USA: NYSE says January short interest falls.
newsitem.headline: NYSE says January short interest falls.

text.p: The New York Stock Exchange said on Tuesday that short interest fell 75.2 million shares to 2.80 billion shares, as of January 15, 1997 -- breaking a string of consecutive months with record high short interest.
On December 19, 1996, the New York Stock Exchange reported short interest of 2.88 billion shares as of December 13, 1996.
January's decrease in short interest is the first since July 1996, breaking a string of record setting highs from August 1996, the New York Stock Exchange said.
The exchange reports short interest, an indication of the number of investors that expect stock prices to fall, on a monthly basis.
